title: A Circuit Breaker in Seoul, a Breather on Wall Street — Is the Worst Over?
body:
On Friday, the selling in Seoul grew so intense that trading briefly **came to a halt**. The KOSPI triggered a **circuit breaker** (서킷브레이커 — 급락 시 매매 일시 정지) and closed down 6.0% at 5,059.69, which left the index 23.6% below where it had stood 20 trading days earlier. Foreign investors dumped a net 2.77 trillion won of shares, while local institutions bought about 1.7 trillion won. Hours later, however, Wall Street told a different story. Data showed that U.S. employers had added 165,000 jobs in October, a far more **resilient** figure than many had feared. The Nasdaq rose 1.1% to 24,579.42 and the S&P 500 edged up 0.3% to 7,376.86, while the VIX fell 9% to 25.64.

Still, it is far from clear whether this **breather** marks a real turning point. A strong job market is good news for the economy, but it could also make the Federal Reserve less willing to cut rates, so traders may trim their **rate-cut bets** (금리 인하 기대 베팅). Indeed, the 10-year Treasury yield ticked up to 4.86%. Faced with such **conflicting** signals, investors would be wise not to **read too much into** a single calm session. If inflation turns out to be stickier than expected, the relief could vanish as quickly as it arrived. That is why many traders are likely to stay cautious until October's consumer price data comes out on Tuesday night, Korean time. Since mid-October, the KOSPI has staged several sharp rebounds, yet each one has faded within days, and nobody knows what the next inflation number will bring.
ko:
금요일 서울의 매도세는 너무 거세져서 거래가 잠시 멈춰 섰다. 코스피는 서킷브레이커가 발동된 끝에 6.0% 내린 5,059.69에 마감했고, 이로써 지수는 20거래일 전보다 23.6% 낮은 수준이 됐다. 외국인은 2조 7,700억 원어치를 순매도한 반면 국내 기관은 약 1조 7,000억 원을 순매수했다. 그런데 몇 시간 뒤 월가는 전혀 다른 이야기를 들려줬다. 미국 고용주들이 10월에 일자리 16만 5,000개를 늘렸다는 자료가 나왔는데, 많은 이들이 걱정했던 것보다 훨씬 탄탄한 수치였다. 나스닥은 1.1% 오른 24,579.42, S&P 500은 0.3% 오른 7,376.86을 기록했고, VIX는 9% 내린 25.64였다.

그래도 이번 숨 고르기가 진짜 전환점인지는 전혀 분명하지 않다. 고용 시장이 강한 건 경제엔 좋은 소식이지만, 연준이 금리 인하를 덜 서두르게 만들 수도 있어서 트레이더들이 금리 인하 기대 베팅을 줄일 수 있다. 실제로 미 10년물 국채 금리는 4.86%로 소폭 올랐다. 이렇게 엇갈린 신호 앞에서는 하루 조용했던 장에 너무 큰 의미를 두지 않는 게 현명하다. 물가가 예상보다 끈적하게 나오면 안도감은 온 만큼이나 빨리 사라질 수 있다. 그래서 많은 트레이더가 한국 시간 화요일 밤 10월 소비자물가 자료가 나올 때까지 조심스러운 태도를 유지할 가능성이 크다. 10월 중순 이후 코스피는 여러 차례 가파르게 반등했지만 매번 며칠 안에 힘을 잃었고, 다음 물가 숫자가 무엇을 가져올지는 아무도 모른다.

vocab.ko: 서킷브레이커(지수 급락 시 거래를 일시 정지하는 장치)
vocab.en_easy: A rule that stops all trading for a short time when prices fall too fast.
vocab.ex: The KOSPI fell so fast that a circuit breaker was triggered, and nobody could trade for a while.

vocab.en_easy: A short pause or rest after a period of hard work or big moves.
vocab.ex: After three sets of heavy squats, I took a quick breather and drank some water.

vocab.ko: 금리 인하 기대 베팅(시장이 금리 인하를 예상하고 거는 포지션)
vocab.en_easy: Trades or guesses that the central bank will lower interest rates soon.
vocab.ex: After the strong jobs data, traders scaled back their rate-cut bets for December.

vocab.en_easy: Able to stay strong or recover quickly after something bad happens.
vocab.ex: My knees used to hurt after running, but they've become more resilient since I started doing leg work.

vocab.en_easy: Saying or showing different things that do not agree with each other.
vocab.ex: I got conflicting advice — one trainer said to rest, and another said to keep training.
Traffic came to a complete halt on the highway, so our day trip took twice as long.

vocab.ko: ~에 너무 큰 의미를 두다, 지나치게 해석하다
vocab.en_easy: To think something means more than it really does.
vocab.ex: Don't read too much into one good day — the market can turn quickly.

grammar.point: 시간 표현 (until + 현재시제 = 미래 · since + 시점, 주절 현재완료)
grammar.quote: …stay cautious until October's consumer price data comes out on Tuesday night … Since mid-October, the KOSPI has staged several sharp rebounds…
grammar.explain_ko: ① until/when/before 같은 '시간 부사절' 안에서는 미래 일이라도 현재시제를 쓴다(comes out ○ / will come out ×). ② since + 과거 시점이 오면 '그때부터 지금까지' 이어진 일이므로 주절은 현재완료(has staged)를 쓴다. 과거형(staged)을 쓰면 '지금까지'라는 연결이 끊긴다.
examples: I'm going to wait until the CPI number comes out before I buy anything.
(OPIc) Since I started doing deadlifts last spring, my lower back has gotten a lot stronger.

grammar.point: 간접의문문 (whether / what + 주어 + 동사 — 의문문이 문장 속 명사절로)
grammar.quote: it is far from clear whether this breather marks a real turning point … nobody knows what the next inflation number will bring.
grammar.explain_ko: 의문문이 다른 문장 안에 들어가면 어순이 '의문사(whether) + 주어 + 동사'로 바뀐다. Does this breather mark …? → whether this breather marks … / What will the number bring? → what the number will bring. 의문사가 없는 Yes/No 질문은 whether(if)로 연결한다.
examples: Nobody knows whether the rebound will last into next week.
(OPIc) I'm not sure what the gym looked like back then, but I remember it was really small.

tense.sentence: Data showed that U.S. employers had added 165,000 jobs in October.
tense.why_ko: 자료가 '보여준' 것(금요일 발표)보다 일자리가 '늘어난' 것(10월)이 먼저 → 더 이전 과거는 had p.p.

tense.sentence: Since mid-October, the KOSPI has staged several sharp rebounds, yet each one has faded within days.
tense.why_ko: since + 시점 → 10월 중순부터 지금까지 이어지는 기간의 경험·결과 → 현재완료. 특정 과거 하루(on Friday)였다면 과거형.

review.q: When the typhoon hit the coast, the small shops along the beach ________ the damage. 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
review.exp_ko: 태풍 피해를 '가장 크게 입었다' → bore the brunt of(①). ② ~을 앞장서다 ③ ~을 만회하다 ④ ~에 익숙해지다 — 모두 동사구지만 '피해'와 짝이 안 맞는다.

review.q: "The new owner managed to turn the struggling café around within a year." 밑줄 친 turn ~ around 와 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: sold the café to a bigger chain
moved the café to a new location
kept the café exactly as it was
review.exp_ko: struggling(장사가 안 되던) 가게를 turn around = 다시 잘 되게 만들다(②). ①③ 가게를 팔거나 옮긴 건 '살린' 게 아니고 ④ 그대로 둔 건 반전이 없다.

review.q: I was about to ________ at the 8 km mark, but my friend kept cheering me on, so I finished the whole 10K. 빈칸에 가장 알맞은 것은?
review.exp_ko: but … so I finished(그래도 끝까지 뛰었다)와 대조 → '포기하려던 참' = throw in the towel(③). ① 속도를 올리다 ② 다시 힘이 나다 ④ 페이스를 찾다 — 모두 긍정이라 but 뒤 '완주'와 대조가 안 된다.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 문맥상 가장 적절한 것은?
"Faced with such conflicting signals, investors would be wise not to ________ a single calm session."
quiz.exp_ko: 엇갈린 신호 → 하루 조용한 장을 '과대 해석하지 말라' = read too much into(②). ① 밀린 것을 따라잡다 ③ ~로 돈을 벌다(이익 실현) — '현명하지 않다'는 문맥과 안 맞음 ④ ~을 승인하다 — 장(session)을 승인한다는 건 말이 안 된다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"Since mid-October, the KOSPI ①has staged several rebounds. Investors want to know ②whether the bounce will last, and many plan to wait until the CPI data ③will come out. ④Faced with conflicting signals, they are staying cautious."
choices: ② whether the bounce will last
quiz.exp_ko: until 이 이끄는 시간 부사절에서는 미래라도 현재시제 → comes out 이 맞다(③). ① since + 시점 → 현재완료 ✓ ② 간접의문문 whether + 주어 + 동사 ✓(주절 밖 명사절이라 will 가능) ④ 투자자가 신호에 '직면한' 수동 관계 → 과거분사 Faced ✓.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? (본문 전체)
choices: A strong U.S. jobs report lifted stocks, but its mixed implications mean Friday's calm does not yet confirm a turnaround.
A strong U.S. jobs report removed the main risk, so investors no longer need to wait for the coming inflation data.
Korean institutions triggered Friday's circuit breaker by selling heavily, while foreign investors bought the dip.
The VIX's 9% decline proves that the sell-off in Seoul ended as soon as Wall Street rebounded on Friday.
quiz.exp_ko: 주제문 'it is far from clear whether this breather marks a real turning point' + 고용 호조의 양면(금리 인하 기대 축소) → ①. ② 오히려 CPI까지 조심하라고 했다 ③ 매도는 외국인, 매수는 기관 — 주체가 뒤바뀜 ④ 'proves'·'ended'는 본문의 신중한 결론과 반대.

quiz.q: [내용 일치] 다음 중 글의 내용으로 추론할 수 있는 것은?
choices: 미 10년물 금리는 고용 지표 발표 뒤 하락했다.

talk.topic: Circuit breaker in Seoul, rebound in New York — 고용 서프라이즈 뒤 월요일 아침 코스피는?
talk.setting_ko: 월요일 아침 출근길, 같은 팀 동료와 주말 동안의 시장 뉴스를 이야기한다.

dialogue.en: Did you see what happened on Friday? The KOSPI hit a circuit breaker and closed down 6%.
dialogue.ko: 금요일에 무슨 일 있었는지 봤어? 코스피가 서킷브레이커 걸리고 6% 빠져서 끝났잖아.

dialogue.en: I know. I checked my account at lunch and, well, it was a mixed bag — some of my stocks held up, but my chip names got crushed.
dialogue.ko: 알아. 점심 때 계좌 봤는데, 음, 뒤죽박죽이더라 — 몇 개는 버텼는데 반도체 종목들은 박살 났어.

dialogue.en: At least Wall Street bounced that night. The jobs report came in strong, and the Nasdaq was up about 1%.
dialogue.ko: 그래도 그날 밤 월가는 반등했어. 고용 지표가 강하게 나와서 나스닥이 1% 정도 올랐고.

dialogue.en: That's a silver lining, I guess. But strong jobs could mean fewer rate cuts, right?
dialogue.ko: 그나마 다행이네. 근데 고용이 강하면 금리 인하가 줄어들 수도 있는 거잖아?

dialogue.en: Exactly. That's why I don't want to get ahead of myself. CPI comes out Tuesday night.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 그래서 너무 앞서 나가고 싶진 않아. 화요일 밤에 CPI가 나오거든.

dialogue.en: So are you going to cut your losses or hang on?
dialogue.ko: 그럼 손절할 거야, 아니면 버틸 거야?

dialogue.en: On paper, I'm down a lot, but I'm not selling into a panic. I'll decide after the CPI.
dialogue.ko: 평가상으론 많이 잃었는데, 공포에 휩쓸려 팔진 않을 거야. CPI 보고 정할래.

dialogue.en: Sounds reasonable. Let's grab a coffee and not look at the screen for ten minutes.
dialogue.ko: 괜찮은 생각이네. 커피나 사고 10분만 화면 보지 말자.

expressions.ko: 좋은 것과 나쁜 것이 뒤섞인 것
expressions.ex: The earnings season has been a mixed bag so far.

expressions.when_ko: 안 좋은 일 속에서 위안거리를 말할 때
expressions.ex: The trip got canceled, but the silver lining is that I saved some money.

expressions.when_ko: 아직 확인 안 된 일을 미리 확신할 때 경계하며
expressions.ex: Let's not get ahead of ourselves — one good day doesn't make a trend.

expressions.ko: 손절하다, 더 손해 보기 전에 그만두다
expressions.ex: The movie was so boring that we cut our losses and left halfway.
On paper, I'm down 10%, but I haven't sold anything yet.

your_turn.q_en: When you hear mixed news — some good, some bad — how do you decide what to do with your investments?
your_turn.hint_ko: 현재 습관(I usually ~) + 이유(because) + 이번 주 계획(until + 현재시제). 'a mixed bag', 'get ahead of myself' 넣기.
your_turn.sample_answer: Well, when the news is a mixed bag, I try not to get ahead of myself. I usually write down the one or two numbers that really matter and wait until they come out. For example, this week I'm going to hold off until the CPI data is released on Tuesday. On paper, I've lost quite a bit, but I don't think selling in a panic is a good idea. I'd rather make a calm decision with all the information.

talk.topic: 가을 단풍 당일치기 — 차 막힘 피하기 vs 기차 타기 (Background Survey #56 국내 여행)
talk.setting_ko: 친구와 이번 주말 단풍 구경 당일치기를 계획한다. 차로 갈지 기차로 갈지 정하는 중.

dialogue.en: The leaves are supposed to be at their peak this weekend. Want to do a day trip to Chuncheon?
dialogue.ko: 이번 주말에 단풍이 절정이래. 춘천으로 당일치기 갈래?

dialogue.en: I'm in. But if we drive, the highway's going to be packed.
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 근데 차로 가면 고속도로 엄청 막힐 거야.

dialogue.en: We could leave at like six in the morning to beat the traffic.
dialogue.ko: 차 막히는 거 피하려면 아침 6시쯤 출발하면 되지.

dialogue.en: Six? That's brutal. What about the ITX train? It only takes about an hour.
dialogue.ko: 6시? 그건 너무 가혹해. ITX 기차는 어때? 한 시간 정도밖에 안 걸려.

dialogue.en: Good idea. And there's a famous dakgalbi place near the station, so we can kill two birds with one stone.
dialogue.ko: 좋은 생각이야. 역 근처에 유명한 닭갈비집도 있으니까 일석이조네.

dialogue.en: Perfect. Do you want to hike first or eat first?
dialogue.ko: 완벽해. 등산 먼저 할래, 밥 먼저 먹을래?

dialogue.en: I'm easy. Whatever works for you.
dialogue.ko: 난 아무거나 괜찮아. 너 편한 대로 해.

dialogue.en: Then hike first. I want to actually earn that dakgalbi.
dialogue.ko: 그럼 등산 먼저. 그 닭갈비는 땀 흘리고 먹고 싶어.

expressions.ex: The cherry blossoms in Jinhae are at their peak in early April.
The gym is always packed at 7 p.m.

expressions.when_ko: 교통 체증을 피하려고 일찍·늦게 출발할 때
expressions.ex: We left before sunrise to beat the traffic.

expressions.en: kill two birds with one stone
expressions.ko: 일석이조, 한 번에 두 가지를 해내다
expressions.when_ko: 한 행동으로 두 목적을 이룰 때
expressions.ex: I walk to work, so I kill two birds with one stone — exercise and commuting.
Pizza or burgers? — I'm easy, you pick.

your_turn.q_en: Tell me about a short trip you took recently. How did you get there, and what did you do?
your_turn.hint_ko: 과거 시제로 출발-이동-한 일-느낌 순서. 'beat the traffic', 'be at its peak', 'kill two birds with one stone' 중 2개.
your_turn.sample_answer: Last fall, I took a day trip to Gapyeong with a couple of friends. We left really early to beat the traffic, and it actually worked — we got there in about an hour. The autumn leaves were at their peak, so the whole mountain looked red and orange. We hiked for about two hours and then had grilled fish by the river. It was kind of like killing two birds with one stone, because we got some exercise and some really good food. I was exhausted on the way home, but it was totally worth it.

opic.survey_topic: 헬스 (Background Survey #51) · 월요일 콤보: 묘사 → 루틴 → 과거 경험

combo.q_en: In your background survey, you indicated that you go to a gym. Tell me about the gym you usually go to. Where is it, and what does it look like? Please describe it in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 서베이에서 헬스장에 다닌다고 하셨네요. 주로 가는 헬스장에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼나요? 최대한 자세히 묘사해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(위치·첫인상 한 줄) → 본문 ① 공간 배치(입구-유산소 구역-프리웨이트 구역, 방향 표현) ② 분위기·사람·시간대 ③ 좋아하는 점/아쉬운 점 + 이유 → 마무리(그래서 계속 다닌다). 90초~2분. 채점: 현재시제 일관, 공간을 '지도처럼' 그리는 구체 묘사, 문단 연결어(On top of that, The thing is).
combo.model_answer: Okay, so the gym I usually go to is just a five-minute walk from my apartment, on the second floor of a building right above a convenience store. When you walk in, the front desk is on your left, and right behind it there's a long row of treadmills and bikes facing the windows. Honestly, that's the part I like least, because it gets really hot in the afternoon. But if you keep walking toward the back, that's where the free-weight area is — you know, the squat racks, a deadlift platform, and dumbbells all the way up to forty kilos. The floor there is covered with thick black rubber mats, so it's not too loud when people drop the weights. On top of that, there's a big mirror on the wall, which is really useful for checking my form. The thing is, it gets pretty packed around seven p.m., so I try to go either early in the morning or after nine. It's not fancy or anything, but it has everything I need, so I've been going there for almost three years.

key_phrases.en: It's just a five-minute walk from ~
If you keep walking toward the back, that's where ~
which is really useful for checking my form
It's not fancy or anything, but ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 '크고 깨끗해요'로 끝나고, IH는 '입구→안쪽' 동선으로 공간을 그리며, AL은 거기에 '왜 그게 좋은지/싫은지' 이유와 시간대 같은 생활 디테일을 붙인다.

combo.q_en: What do you usually do when you work out at the gym? Tell me about your typical routine, from the moment you arrive until you leave.
combo.q_ko: 헬스장에서 운동할 때 보통 무엇을 하나요? 도착한 순간부터 나갈 때까지 평소 루틴을 말해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(주 몇 회·분할 방식) → 본문 ① 워밍업(부위 이름) ② 메인 운동 2개(근육 이름+세트·횟수, progressive overload) ③ 마무리(스트레칭·기록) → 마무리(요즘 목표). 현재시제 습관 표현(usually, always, once a week) + 순서어(First, After that, Once I'm done). 지난 시험 전략 그대로 '근육 이름'으로 구체성 확보.
combo.model_answer: Well, I usually work out four times a week, and I follow a simple split — upper body one day, lower body the next. Let me walk you through a leg day, because that's my favorite. First, I spend about ten minutes on the bike just to get my heart rate up, and then I do some light stretches for my hips and hamstrings. After that, I move on to the main lift, which is the squat. I do four sets of six to eight reps, and I try to add a little weight every week — that's called progressive overload. Next, I do Romanian deadlifts, which really hit my hamstrings and glutes, and then I finish with leg extensions for my quads. I mean, by the end, my legs are basically shaking. Once I'm done, I always write down my weights in an app, because if I don't, I honestly can't remember what I lifted last week. The whole thing takes about an hour and ten minutes. These days, my goal is to squat my body weight for eight reps by the end of the year.

key_phrases.en: I move on to the main lift, which is ~
really hit my hamstrings and glutes
by the end, my legs are basically shaking

combo.level_up_ko: IH→AL 차이는 '순서어 + 근육 이름 + 이유'의 반복: 'I do X, which hits Y, because Z' 구조를 2번 이상 넣고, 마지막에 미래 목표(by the end of the year)로 시제를 하나 더 보여준다.

combo.q_en: Can you tell me about a memorable experience you had while working out? Maybe something unexpected or funny happened. What happened, and how did you feel about it?
combo.q_ko: 운동하다가 있었던 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요. 예상치 못했거나 웃긴 일이 있었을 수도 있죠. 무슨 일이 있었고, 어떤 기분이었나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·어디 한 줄) → 배경(그 전 상황, 과거완료 1번) → 사건(시간 순서, 대화 한 줄 인용) → 감정·결과 → 교훈(그 뒤로 달라진 점 — since + 현재완료). 과거시제 일관이 핵심, 마지막 한두 문장만 현재로.
combo.model_answer: Oh, I actually have a pretty funny one. It was about two years ago, on a Saturday morning. I'd been stuck at the same deadlift weight for almost two months, and I was getting really frustrated. So that day, I decided to go for a new personal record — a hundred and forty kilos. I chalked up my hands, took a deep breath, and pulled... and to my surprise, it went up! I was so excited that I let out this huge yell, like, way too loud. And then I realized the whole gym had gone completely silent and everyone was staring at me. An older guy on the bench just gave me a thumbs-up and said, "Nice pull, but maybe a little quieter next time." I was so embarrassed, but at the same time, I couldn't stop smiling. Looking back, that moment taught me that patience really pays off. Since then, I've stopped trying to lift heavy every single week, and I've focused more on my form and recovery. And, yeah, I celebrate a little more quietly now.

key_phrases.en: I'd been stuck at ~ for almost two months
I was so embarrassed, but at the same time, ~
Looking back, that moment taught me that ~
key_phrases.ko: 돌이켜 보면 그 순간이 ~라는 걸 가르쳐 줬어요

combo.level_up_ko: AL은 '사건' 앞에 배경(had been stuck — 과거완료)을 깔고, 대사 한 줄 인용으로 장면을 살리고, 끝에 Since then + 현재완료로 '지금의 나'까지 연결한다.

useful.en: Oh, I actually have a pretty funny one.
useful.ko: 아, 저 꽤 웃긴 얘기가 하나 있어요.
useful.when_ko: 경험 질문 첫 문장 — 바로 이야기 모드로 들어갈 때
과거 경험 답변을 교훈·감정으로 마무리할 때

opic.practice_ko: 오늘은 2번(루틴)만 2분 녹음: 근육 이름 4개(hamstrings·glutes·quads·hips)와 순서어(First·After that·Next·Once I'm done)를 모두 넣었는지 체크. 다시 듣고 'which ~' 이유 문장이 2번 미만이면 한 번 더 녹음.
